title: Sister Death
hookLine: Francis, near the end of his life, adds a verse to his Canticle of the Creatures praising Sister Death

lines: A SONG OF THE WHOLE HOUSEHOLD.
ONE MORE NAME, NEAR THE END.
cards: Brother Sun. Sister Moon and the stars. Brother Wind.
Sister Water. Brother Fire. Mother Earth.
These are the names in a song by Francis of Assisi, written in the everyday Italian of his region rather than in church Latin.
It's called the Canticle of the Creatures, or the Canticle of the Sun, and it praises God for each of them, as if the whole world were a household.

teach.b: Francis doesn't praise the sun as a lamp or water as a resource. He gives each a place at the table. Sister Water is useful and humble and precious and pure.
Brother Fire is beautiful and strong. Everything in the song is kin.
The new verse praises God for our Sister Bodily Death, from whom no living person can escape. Francis doesn't say death is pleasant, or optional, or not real.
He says it is certain, and then he calls it sister, the same word he used for the moon.
It isn't sentimental, either. The verse warns: woe to those who die in mortal sin. And it calls blessed those whom death finds doing God's holy will, for the second death will do them no harm.
Some readers hear in that phrase an echo of the book of Revelation. For Francis, a sister can still be serious. An enemy is something you fight.
A sister comes whether you are ready or not, but she belongs to the household.
Paul called death the last enemy; Francis calls it sister. Both words come from Christian voices.
Death is the same in both. What changes is where it sits: outside the door, or at the table.

how: Franciscans and other Christians sing or pray the Canticle of the Creatures, and in Franciscan communities the death of a brother or sister is sometimes spoken of as the coming of Sister Death.

games.q: you're Francis, ill near the end of your life. your song already praises sun, moon, wind, water, fire and earth. what do you add?
o: a verse asking to be spared.
a verse praising God for our Sister Bodily Death.
games.why: tradition says he added Sister Death to the family, the same word he used for the moon.

practice: Bring to mind one ending that has already happened, not a raw loss but a finished thing: a school year, a job, a move, a friendship that ran its course, a habit you finally put down.
Look at what it made room for, and thank it, as if it had been a sister walking you to a door. If you pray, you can offer that thanks to God, as Francis did.

wordCard.voice: Sister Death: Francis of Assisi's name for bodily death in his Canticle of the Creatures, certain and unavoidable, and still counted as family. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: a place at the table. Francis gave even the last guest a family name. Go gently.
